name: kill-process
title: Kill Process
description: List what is running — apps, helpers and daemons — sorted by the memory or CPU it is costing you, and quit or force-kill it. Reads /bin/ps directly, shows each process under its owning app's icon, and tells you plainly when a process belongs to root and cannot be signalled without sudo.
author: sujha

commands.name: kill-process
commands.title: Kill Process
commands.subtitle: Activity Monitor
commands.description: Find a running process by name and quit or force-kill it.

preferences.name: scope
preferences.title: Default Scope
preferences.description: Which processes the list opens on. Apps are the ones with a window; Mine is every process running as you; All includes root and system daemons.

preferences.name: sort
preferences.title: Default Sort
preferences.description: Memory answers "what is eating my RAM"; CPU answers "what is spinning my fans". Toggle it in the list with ⌘S.

preferences.name: confirmForceKill
preferences.title: Confirm Force Kill
preferences.description: Ask before sending SIGKILL. A force-kill gives the process no chance to save, so this is on by default; plain Quit (SIGTERM) never asks.
preferences.label: Ask before sending SIGKILL
